examples.whisper_text: I guess a button makes a bit more sense, because otherwise you don't really know what happens then.
examples.human_text: I GUESS A BUTTON BUTTON MAKES A BIT MORE SENSE 'CAUSE OTHERWISE YOU DON'T REALLY KNOW THAT OH WHAT IF I RIGHT CLICK NOW WHAT HAPPENS THEN
examples.notes: The reference asks what would happen if someone right-clicked. Whisper drops the right-click action from the end of the sentence.

examples.whisper_text: Can we integrate the data text and the subtitles in one button?
examples.human_text: CAN WE USE CAN'T WE INTEGRATE THE TELETEXT AND THE SUBTITLES IN ONE BUTTON
examples.notes: The reference names teletext as the feature to combine with subtitles. Whisper writes “data text”, obscuring which feature the speaker meant.

examples.case_title: Matching words still earn a review slot
examples.whisper_text: Very interesting start of the meeting.
examples.human_text: VERY INTERESTING START OF THE MEETING
examples.notes: The generated transcript and reference use the same words. Both methods allocated a review slot even though the recorded WER was zero.

examples.whisper_text: This skin fixture shows sexual dim of prism with the male more brightly colored than the female.
examples.human_text: This kingfisher shows sexual dimorphism, with the male more brightly coloured than the female.
examples.notes: Whisper turns “kingfisher” into “skin fixture” and “sexual dimorphism” into “sexual dim of prism”, distorting the subject and the term that explains the difference between males and females.

examples.case_title: A time reference becomes a country
examples.whisper_text: They repeated the same procedure on the way back to Jordan and Israel.
examples.human_text: They repeated the same procedure on the way back to Jordan the next day.
examples.notes: Whisper replaces “the next day” with “and Israel”, adding a destination to the return trip and dropping when it occurred.

examples.whisper_text: Which Moses justified in resisting the gypsum taskmaster
examples.human_text: WAS MOSES JUSTIFIED IN RESISTING THE EGYPTIAN TASKMASTER
examples.notes: The reference asks whether Moses was justified in resisting the Egyptian taskmaster. Whisper changes “was” to “which” and “Egyptian” to “gypsum”, altering the question and the description of the taskmaster.

examples.whisper_text: The claw seemed superfluous on first sight.
examples.human_text: THE CLAUSE SEEMS SUPERFLUOUS ON FIRST SIGHT
examples.notes: Whisper writes “claw” for “clause” and “seemed” for “seems”. The noun change alters what the sentence is talking about. Both methods left the clip outside their review budgets.
